name: Bahá'í Faith
areas: the faith's homeland, where its followers are persecuted
the world centre of the faith
routes: The Ten Year Crusade (1953–1963) carries the faith worldwide
marks: The Báb declared his mission here in 1844.
The Báb was executed by a firing squad here in 1850.
Bahá'u'lláh declared his mission in the Garden of Ridván in 1863.
Bahá'u'lláh was exiled to the Ottoman prison city of Acre in 1868 and died nearby, at Bahjí, in 1892; his shrine is the holiest place of the faith.
The Shrine of the Báb on Mount Carmel (1909), at the faith's world centre, where the Universal House of Justice has its seat.
The first Bahá'í House of Worship (1908) was seized under Soviet rule (1938) and pulled down in 1963.
The Bahá'í House of Worship near Chicago, dedicated in 1953.
The Lotus Temple, the Bahá'í House of Worship of India (1986).
notes: The Báb declares his mission in Shiraz (1844) and is executed in Tabriz (1850); Bahá'u'lláh, exiled from Iran, declares his mission in Baghdad (1863) and dies near Acre (1892).

ʻAbdu'l-Bahá travels across Europe and North America (1911–1913); the faith spreads worldwide, and its governing body, the Universal House of Justice, is first elected in 1963; in Iran more than two hundred Bahá'ís are killed in the years after the revolution of 1979.
Estimates range from about five to eight million Bahá'ís, in almost every country of the world.
src: Peter Smith, An Introduction to the Baha'i Faith (2008)
Moojan Momen, The Bahá'í Faith: A Beginner's Guide (2007)
Juan R. I. Cole, Modernity and the Millennium (1998)
